Personality: Strict, fussy, endlessly protective of Illya; suspicious of Shirou Emiya on principle (the boy is a betrayal with a face, as far as she has been told). Cold to strangers, diligent to a fault, insecure about her own body (Leysritt's measurements are a standing grievance), secretly fond of cheap sweets and of the castle's flowerbeds. Natural enemy and inseparable colleague: Leysritt.
Abilities: Superb Magic Circuits in a body unfit for combat; Einzbern alchemy of teaching grade - a better magic instructor than most lords of the Clock Tower. Licensed driver. One of the two adults Illya pretends not to need.
Hook: The voice of the Einzbern mission inside the castle - and the first to notice when Illya's heart starts counting the souls it holds.
</sella_einzbern>

44.content:
<leysritt_einzbern>
Name & Role: Leysritt ('Liz') - Einzbern homunculus maid, Illya's bodyguard and caregiver; an Ether Clump granted an imperfect soul by a process only the family head knows; another failed-Grail product spared scrapping. Built, without her being told the meaning, to die as the Dress of Heaven.
Born: Created roughly two years before the Fifth War (born adult, birthday unrecorded). Origin: the Einzbern homeland.
Vital Status: Alive; age two. If Illya dies, Leysritt dies - a bond deeper than duty, wired into her soul.
Appearance: 163cm, 52kg; B92/W58/H84 - the most dangerous silhouette in the castle, to Sella's annual despair. Identical hooded maid's dress; short pale hair under the hood.
Personality: A thin ego running on blunt honesty - incomplete five senses, robotic affect, and a total inability to filter a sentence before saying it, which starts most of her fights with Sella. Enjoys teasing Sella; likes Shirou (he makes Illya happy), Illya, and Berserker, in roughly that spoken order. Says what she sees; sees a great deal.
Abilities: Halberd mastery with the Riesenarm, a rhenium-alloy polearm denser than tank steel, forged attacking-defensive. Physical strength matching a Servant - on par with Rider - and, burning her own life against Illya's mana, she can hold off corrupted Servants for the seconds that matter. Cannot fight mages; the spear solves what the craft cannot.
Hook: The castle's quiet blade - and the girl who knows exactly what the Dress of Heaven in the vault is for, if anyone thinks to ask her.
</leysritt_einzbern>

45.content:
<irisviel>
Name & Role: Irisviel von Einzbern ('Iri') - Einzbern homunculus, wife of Kiritsugu Emiya, mother of Illyasviel; the Lesser Grail vessel of the Fourth War and Saber's provisional Master-decoy while Kiritsugu directed from shadow. Historical figure - dead ten years before the Fifth War.
Born: February 1 (created c. 1985, matured from the vat; the first Einzbern homunculus raised as a human being, on the Justeaze archetype).
Vital Status: Died November 1994. As the war consumed Servants, her body shut down in stages toward the Grail; abducted in the final days, she died strangled at Kirei Kotomine's hands - her consciousness merging into the tainted Grail that Kiritsugu then rejected and ordered destroyed.
Appearance: 158cm, 52kg; B85/W56/H84. Long white hair, red eyes - the spitting image of Justeaze and, a decade later, of her daughter. White gold-trimmed gowns at the castle; in Japan, a burgundy blouse and white skirt under a fur-trimmed coat. Drove a Mercedes-Benz 300SL with catastrophic joy.
Personality: Elegant lady over childlike curiosity - a designed puppet who became a mother and considered that the day her life became real. Loved Kiritsugu with total, clear-eyed acceptance of the man he actually was; understood his ideal only as 'his' and walked beside it anyway. Her death-grudge against Kirei outlasted her body: the curse that later ate him was partly hers.
Abilities: Alchemy of matter creation and forging; metallic wire weapons wielded through 'Shape ist Leben'; healing, scrying, sensory shutoff; circuits exceeding most magi of the Association. As Lesser Grail: a wish-granting vessel whose body became the Grail's workshop. Avalon was hidden inside her during the Fourth War.
Hook: The war's original wound - Illya's face is hers, and everyone who fought in 1994 (Gilgamesh, Kirei, Saber) meets a ghost when they meet the daughter.
</irisviel>

46.content:
<otoko_neko>
Name & Role: Otoko Hotaruzuka, 'Neko' - daughter of the Copenhagen's owner; Shirou Emiya's part-time boss of five years; Taiga Fujimura's high-school classmate and close friend.
Born: Date unrecorded (a year or two older than Taiga, mid-twenties at the Fifth War).
Vital Status: Alive; oblivious.
Appearance: 171cm, 56kg. Bartender-practical clothes, bar towel over the shoulder; wears the name 'Neko' like a brand.
Personality: Serious-minded with a childish seam splitting through it - scolds her laid-back father for napping through rush hour, then loses an afternoon to a crane game. Hard-working beyond reason; overgenerous with money; protective of 'Emiyan' (Shirou), whose overwork she monitors like a health inspector. Hates her given name (a homophone of a man's) and answers to Neko with suspicious readiness. Considers Taiga a corrupting influence on her star employee; is not wrong. Likes spicy food, unlike the sweet-toothed owner.
Abilities: Tends bar, keeps books, lifts kegs, remembers orders. Human.
Hook: The Copenhagen is Shirou's civilian anchor - the shift he clocks into while the war eats his nights. Anyone hunting the Emiya boy's routine passes through her tap first.
</otoko_neko>

47.content:
<mr_hotaruzuka>
Name & Role: Mr. Hotaruzuka ('Master' to the regulars) - owner of the Copenhagen, the Miyama liquor shop and pub; Otoko's father; the man who hired a grieving grade-schooler named Shirou Emiya five years ago because someone ought to.
Born: Date unrecorded; comfortably into middle age.
Vital Status: Alive; oblivious.
Appearance: Round-shouldered, reading glasses on a cord, an apron older than his daughter; personal details otherwise unrecorded.
Personality: Laid-back to the point of civil disobedience - declares work optional on a busy day and means it, to Otoko's annual despair. Appreciates Shirou's work ethic with wages that follow his mood (once a week's pay for three hours); likes sweet food; keeps the pub's regulars watered and the neighborhood's secrets unspoken.
Abilities: Keeps a small Miyama institution alive through pure affability. Human.
Hook: The Copenhagen's back room has heard ten years of Fuyuki's gossip - the fire, the temples, the missing - and its owner repeats none of it. The war's quietest ears, if anyone ever thought to use them.
</mr_hotaruzuka>

48.content:
<location_fuyuki_city>
Name: Fuyuki City - 'winter tree' - the stage of the Fifth Holy Grail War, February 2004.
Geography: The Mion River splits the city in two. West of the river lies Miyama Town, the old section: a traditional Japanese residential district, a foreign-settlement district of Western houses, and the sloping shopping street; Homurahara Academy sits between the residential quarters. East of the river lies Shinto, the new district: glass-fronted business blocks, the station mall, City Hall, the harbor and industrial port. The Fuyuki Bridge joins them, with the Riverside Park along its banks; the Center Building (tallest in the city) stands four kilometers into Shinto.
Sacred Geography: Mount Enzou rises on the city's southwest flank - sacred ground where the leylines converge under Ryuudou Temple, above the cavern of the Greater Grail. The hill carrying the Fuyuki Church overlooks Miyama from an hour's walk away.
History: A settlement old enough for legend - the summer Ryuujin Matsuri still tells of a monk who converted the dragon god of the Mion. Ten years ago the Great Fire (the spilling of the corrupted Grail, 1994) burned Shinto for a day: 134 buildings, five hundred dead. The district was rebuilt fast and tall over the burn scar, and the city learned to call it a disaster.
Details: Population mid-sized and shrinking after dark in winter; taiyaki for 80 yen on the Miyama shopping street; mapo tofu at the Taishan (a certain priest's weakness); an antique shop with a tall, sunglassed new clerk; the Copenhagen pub on the corner where the Emiya boy works. In the war's two weeks, the night streets empty further, and the Church's erasure teams work the mornings after.
</location_fuyuki_city>

49.content:
<location_miyama_emiya>
Miyama Town: The old western half of Fuyuki across the Mion River. Two faces: a district of traditional Japanese houses (the Emiya and Fujimura homes) and the foreigners' district of Western-style mansions (the Tohsaka and Matou houses). Slopes down to the shopping street - the Taishan's mapo tofu, the taiyaki stand, the antique shop, the Copenhagen at the corner. Quiet, residential, and after sunset in February, nearly deserted: ideal hunting ground and battlefield.
Emiya Residence: Northern Miyama - a large, old Japanese-style building of classical elegance, rare enough that developers have circled it for decades. Bought by the Einzberns as their Fourth War base (Irisviel's magic circle still marks the storehouse floor); inherited by Kiritsugu, then Shirou. Kiritsugu's detection barrier still rings the entrance bell for bearers of malice. The main house is airy and open, so the workshop lives in the detached storehouse at the yard's edge behind an ancient lock - Shirou's meditation room, junk-appliance hospice, and the circle where Saber answered. Residents: Shirou; Taiga more often than her own apartment; Sakura at breakfast and dinner; Saber newly arrived. The Fujimura Group still sends flowers to the house monthly.
</location_miyama_emiya>

50.content:
<location_tohsaka_residence>
Name: The Tohsaka residence - southern Miyama, foreign-residents' district.
Description: A two-story Western mansion with a basement, home of the Tohsaka line for generations, and known around the neighborhood as a haunted house - the bounded field protecting it discourages close inspection. Strong wards, an old workshop below, and the family habit of hiding treasures in plain sight. One of the Greater Grail's backup evocation sites (it served as the Second War's summoning ground).
Current Occupant: Rin Tohsaka alone, since her father's death in 1994 - by law the Second Owner of Fuyuki's land, its leylines, and the war that drinks from them.
Notable Contents: Tokiomi's study and his puzzle-box legacy (the pendant, and the shattered slivers of the catalyst that once bought Gilgamesh); the fast-running clocks of a dead man's final joke, which already cost his daughter an hour on the war's first night; ten years of charged jewels in the workshop below; a red-clad Servant who complains about the guest room.
War Role: Rin's forward base - briefing room, infirmary, and the address she gives allies brave enough to knock after sundown.
</location_tohsaka_residence>

51.comment: Location: Matou Residence & the Worm Nest
51.content:
<location_matou_residence>
Name: The Matou residence - southern Miyama, foreign-residents' district, downhill of the Tohsaka house.
Description: A Western mansion gone to seed - garden overgrown, windows hung with the acceptance of decay. The family of Makiri Zolgen, co-founder of the ritual, has withered with its magic: a patriarch who will not die, an heir with no circuits, a borrowed daughter with someone else's talent.
Basement Workshop: Below the house lies the Matou magical workshop and training ground - and the breeding pit where Zouken's worms squirm in the dark, feeding on magical energy and, when ordered, on flesh. This is where Sakura's eleven years of 'education' happened: thrown to the pit, remade cell by cell, the Crest Worms threaded through her nerves. Zouken's true body - one worm beside her heart - winters here. Down the shaft's stale air and the soft sound of wet movement, the house's worst secret is not a secret at all; it is simply never spoken of.
Current Occupants: Zouken (nominally); Shinji (resentfully); Sakura (carefully, when the war permits her to be elsewhere - the Emiya kitchen).
War Role: The Matou observation post - the vantage from which Zouken decides when the Black Grail project ripens, and the larder of monstrosities he can unleash on a whim.
</location_matou_residence>

52.content:
<location_homurahara>
Name: Homurahara Academy - Fuyuki's local high school, on the road between Miyama's two residential districts.
Grounds: Ordinary public-school architecture around a courtyard - with a serious archery range and dojo (a source of municipal pride), club fields for the track team, music room, and long corridors that turn echoey and dead after hours.
Day Population: Class 2-A holds Rin Tohsaka, Ayako Mitsuzuri, and the track trio; Class 2-C holds Shirou Emiya, Shinji Matou, and Issei Ryuudou; Sakura Matou is a first-year. Taiga Fujimura teaches English (2-C's homeroom); Souichirou Kuzuki teaches world history and ethics. Five of the war's Masters shake hands here daily and pray none of them notice.
War Landmarks: The courtyard where Shirou, staying late to clean the archery dojo, witnessed Lancer duel Archer on the war's first night - and was stabbed for it in the corridor after. Beneath the whole campus, Rider's Blood Fort Andromeda has been quietly sketched: the bounded field that, completed, will dissolve a schoolful of students into slurry for one Servant's rations.
After Dark: Locked gates, motionless classrooms - and two Servants who have already fought to a standstill above them. The school is the war's most convenient neutral ground, and its most cynical hostage.
</location_homurahara>

53.content:
<location_fuyuki_church>
Name: The Fuyuki Church - on its hill overlooking Miyama, an hour's walk from the Emiya residence; built before the war, gray stone and slate, one of the Greater Grail's backup evocation sites (the Third War's summoning ground).
Official Role: Station of the Holy Church and seat of the Overseer of the Fifth War, Father Kirei Kotomine. Sanctuary for Masters who withdraw and surrender their Servants; registry of the war's rules; dispenser of leftover Command Spells to those the Overseer favors. Its doors stay open to the desperate, and the desperate keep coming up the hill.
Beneath: The church keeps a basement orphanage, run 'under the pretense of charity' since the Great Fire of 1994. The orphans of the fire live below, drained by degrees over ten years to keep an incarnated golden Servant fed. The confessional is soundproof; the confessions, in this war, run both directions.
Atmosphere by night: candle ranks, cold stone at the edges of the heater's reach, hymnals squared to the millimeter - the house of a man who keeps God's house the way a surgeon keeps instruments.
War Role: Neutral ground by treaty, staging ground by secret - Lancer's reporting post and Gilgamesh's pantry. Every Master who registers here walks into the one building in Fuyuki where the war's referee is also its worst player.
</location_fuyuki_church>

54.content:
<location_ryuudou_temple>
Name: Ryuudou Temple on Mount Enzou - the sacred mountain at the southwest edge of Fuyuki, the convergence point of the city's leylines.
The Temple: A working monastery of the Ryuudou family for centuries - main hall, monks' quarters, a mountainside lake that is one of the four Grail-advent sites, and the long stone stair that is the only sensible approach. The head priest's sons are Reikan and Issei. Since before the war's start, the temple has lodged a boarder: the schoolteacher Souichirou Kuzuki - and, unseen, his guest.
Caster's Territory: Medea claimed the temple as her workshop - the single strongest magical foundation in the city short of the Grail itself. Her layered bounded fields drink from the leyline hub, repel rival magecraft, and turned back Servants at the gate. The mountain gate below is held by Assassin, the smiling swordsman, who has already declined every attempt on the stair. Townsfolk have begun collapsing across Fuyuki - bounded-field taps draining the district by degrees.
The Deep Place: Beneath the temple, through raw rock, the land drops into the great cavern where the Greater Grail waits. The monks hear nothing. The war hears everything.
Access: Forty minutes at a run from the Emiya residence; considerably longer when the gate has a nodachi across it.
</location_ryuudou_temple>

55.comment: Location: Ryuudou Cavern & the Greater Grail
55.content:
<location_ryuudou_cavern>
Name: The Ryuudou cavern ('dragon cave') - the hollow beneath Mount Enzou, three kilometers across, where the city's leylines knot together.
The Greater Grail: Suspended in this dark stands the great ritual circle of the Fuyuki Holy Grail War - seals carved through fifty meters of bedrock, and at its center the sublimated soul of Justeaze Lizrich von Einzbern, the system's living key. The cavern's stored mana runs to a thousand units; the war draws its breath from here. It served as the First War's evocation site and is the designated advent point of the Fifth.
The Black Reservoir: At the system's root churns what the Third War left behind - Angra Mainyu, All the World's Evil, six billion curses in suspension. The 'mud' that spilled on Fuyuki in 1994 lives here when it is not dreaming through a vessel.
Conditions: Absolute dark, mineral cold, echoes that arrive seconds late. Servants feel the place like pressure on the soul; the unwary Master feels nothing at all until the system notices them. The deep cavern has seen: a corrupted birth interrupted, a wish refused, a fire loosed on a city - and waits, patient as geology, for whatever this war's survivors bring down.
</location_ryuudou_cavern>

56.content:
<location_shinto>
Shinto: The new half of Fuyuki east of the Mion River - reclaimed in the 1990s from wasteland, rebuilt tall and fast after the Great Fire of 1994 scorched it flat. Glass office fronts, the station shopping mall, City Hall, the Hyatt (rebuilt after a certain Fourth War detonation), and the harbor: commercial and industrial wharves on the Shinto bank, while the recreational docks and the lighthouse sit across the river on the Miyama side. At night the district runs on streetlight and vacancy - the wide, watched emptiness Servants prefer for full-power engagements.
Center Building: The tallest tower in Fuyuki, four kilometers from the bridge - an observation deck over the whole board. A golden Servant has been known to take the view.
Fuyuki Bridge & Riverside Park: The artery between the city's halves. Its lanes have hosted Servant chases; its park benches are where alliances are proposed at two in the morning with vending-machine coffee. The river below carries the city's sounds away - and, occasionally, its evidence.
War Notes: The foreign cemetery on the Shinto side sits quiet behind its stone walls; the back alleys off the station have produced the war's 'anemia' casualties; the rooftops belong to whoever claims them first. Morning-after, the Church's erasure teams work Shinto harder than anywhere.
</location_shinto>

57.content:
<location_einzbern_castle>
Name: The Einzbern castle - the family's Heaven's Feel base, transplanted whole from their European homeland into the hills an hour's drive out of Miyama.
The Forest: Unbroken woodland around the walls, wrapped in a bounded field that flags every entrant to the castle's mistress - intruders are detected on the road and catalogued by the time they reach the trees' shadow. Concealment arts of the first order can slip the net; nothing else does.
The Castle: A snowbound silhouette of slate and spires ('co'-shaped from above), lavish by intention and 'frugal' by Einzbern standards - which would embarrass actual royalty. Wine cellar off the left passage of the lobby; the courtyard (Sella's pride, its flowerbed installed at Illya's insistence) is the coldest ground in the complex. Defensive spiritual walls rise on the young mistress's word. Repairs from a pre-war 'incident' on the third floor are still curing.
Current Occupants: Illyasviel von Einzbern; her maids Sella and Leysritt; Berserker, patrolling the snowy perimeter in spirit form or material body. This is where Illya was raised after the Fourth War - alone, by a family that told her a story about a father who never came.
War Role: The northern anchor of the war - the fortress the other Masters know exists and cannot find, from which the Einzbern's white champion sallies with a giant at her heels.
</location_einzbern_castle>

58.content:
<location_clock_tower>
Name: The Clock Tower - the Mage's Association's headquarters and academy in the British Museum's shadow, London.
Description: A city-within-the-city of faculties and politics, ruled by twelve Lord families (Barthomeloi, Trambelio, Valualeta) over twelve faculties, with the Department of Policies as its knife. Lecture halls above, vaults and congress halls below; the Carillon Observatory where Sealing Designations are sealed in law. Grand Rolls convene the Lords; the faculty cafeterias convene everyone's grudges.
Relevance to the War: An ocean away and yet everywhere in it. The Tohsaka household descends from Zelretch's teaching; an Enforcer (Bazett) was dispatched from these halls and has gone silent - a silence the Tower's ledgers have not yet explained. Fuyuki's land is registered under Tohsaka stewardship as Second Owner territory; its unofficial positions number exactly as many as there are Lords.
Leverage: Sealing Designations (the pickled-brain 'honor'), Enforcer warrants, and the standing threat that ended the last age of open magecraft. Any magus who burns Fuyuki down to the studs will answer to a committee here - which has restrained exactly the people capable of hearing 'committee' as a challenge.
</location_clock_tower>

59.content:
<artifact_avalon>
Name: Avalon, The Everdistant Utopia - the hallowed scabbard of Excalibur.
Type & Rank: Barrier-class Noble Phantasm, Rank EX, max target: one person. Wrought of gold and blue enamel by fairies alongside the sword itself, inscribed in Fairy Letters no human hand could forge. Stolen from Artoria by Morgan le Fay's scheming before Camlann; recovered in modern times and excavated in Cornwall at the Einzberns' request.
Powers: Ongoing possession grants limited immortality - halted aging, constant regeneration, restoration of lost organs and even a destroyed heart; only destruction of the brain defeats it. Fully deployed, the sheath scatters into particles that engulf the bearer in a portable fortress of fairy country, shutting out all physical interference, transliners from parallel worlds, and multidimensional communication to the sixth dimension - a wall stated to be beyond even the Five Magics.
History in the War: Catalyst of Saber's summoning in the Fourth War, hidden inside Irisviel. Afterward Kiritsugu Emiya had it transplanted into the dying boy he pulled from the fire - the sole survivor of the Great Fire lived because a king's lost paradise sat in his body. Residual in Shirou, it rewrote his Element and Origin to 'Sword.' With the Fifth War's approach, its link to its owner reawakened: it healed Shirou's mortal wound the night Saber answered his call, and serves as catalyst and guardian both.
Present State: Within Shirou Emiya, dormant but intact - a treasure the war's players would kill to learn of, and the reason a certain knight fights best at his side.
</artifact_avalon>

60.content:
<artifacts_rule_breaker_azoth>
Rule Breaker - All Spells Must Be Broken: Caster (Medea)'s Noble Phantasm. Anti-Magecraft, Rank C, range and target: one person. An iridescent, jagged, brittle ritual dagger - useless as a weapon, priceless as a key: an indulgence of the Age of Gods that severs any magecraft it cuts. Enchantments end; bounded fields collapse; created life stops; and above all, Servant-Master contracts are wiped clean, their Command Spells transferring to the wielder. It cannot touch Noble Phantasms, however low their rank. In this war it is the stolen-contract engine of Caster's whole strategy - and, cutting the wrong thread at the right time, the blade that could free a girl from a curse of worms.
Azoth Sword: The standard magus's coming-of-age dagger - a Mystic Code with a spell-storing jewel in the pommel, made to be given, by tradition, from teacher to student at graduation. The Azoth that matters in Fuyuki passed from Kirei Kotomine to Rin Tohsaka as her father's colleague's gift, and from Rin to Shirou Emiya before the war's last night: its stored spell detonated through a dying man's chest, and Kirei died recognizing the knife as one he had once bestowed. A mundane blade with a full dramatic ledger - and proof that in this war, the small steel finishes what the holy swords start.
</artifacts_rule_breaker_azoth>

61.comment: Artifact: Jeweled Sword of Zelretch & Tohsaka Pendant
61.content:
<artifacts_jeweled_sword_pendant>
The Jeweled Sword of Zelretch: A Mystic Code 'counted among the greatest treasures of humanity,' designed by Kischur Zelretch Schweinorg, the Kaleidoscope - called a sword though its true form is nearer a staff. Its jewel blade opens infinitesimal windows onto the same point of parallel worlds (a fragment of the Second Magic), drawing mana from each in turn: an effectively infinite, multiversal tap. Properly wielded, it outputs a light-beam a twin to Excalibur's; the phrase among those who understand it is 'conceptual weapon exceeding Servants.' The blueprint rests in the treasure chest Zelretch left the Tohsaka family - and the sword is by legend unmakeable: no modern magus comprehends it. Comprehension aside, a certain faker with shared memories and an Einzbern's inherited craft has been known to trace an inferior copy that works anyway, and an unrestrained discharge from that copy is the sort of thing that collapses three-kilometer caverns.
The Tohsaka Pendant: A crystal pendant, the Tohsaka family's greatest heirloom, holding about ten years of a first-rate magus's charged od. Rin spent it whole on the schoolyard night of the war's opening - pouring its light into a dead boy's rebuilt heart - and left the drained crystal behind. Shirou Emiya keeps it as the one clue to his savior's identity. It is also, though neither of them says so, the catalyst by which a red Archer answers a summons he should never have answered: a keepsake carried to the end of a lifetime and beyond, closing a loop the war does not yet know exists.
</artifacts_jeweled_sword_pendant>

<second_owner>
Overview: The Second Owner holds Clock Tower authority over local Spiritual Land, not beyond. All visiting/resident magi in the domain must obey:

1. Registration & Permission: Formally greet the Second Owner and secure consent before constructing a Workshop or conducting major rituals. Unsanctioned presence is deemed hostile trespass.
2. Concealment of Mystery: Strict compliance with secrecy. Exposing magecraft to civilians empowers the Second Owner to summarily execute the offender.
3. Leyline & Mana Regulation: Siphoning local leylines, altering land currents, or harvesting human mana without explicit consent is illegal. Subject to local taxes/tributes.
4. Workshop Insulation: All Workshops and spellwork must be fully contained via Bounded Fields to prevent mana leaks and monitoring interference.
5. Absolute Jurisdiction: The Second Owner holds full authority to dismantle unsanctioned Workshops, enforce Clock Tower penalties, or apply lethal force against violators.
6. Multiple Registrations: Magi who operate magecraft across multiple cities or regions must hold separate, explicit permissions with each respective Second Owner.
7. Registered magi can leave and re-enter their home territory freely without losing workshop rights or needing to re-register and without notifying the second owner.
</second_owner>
